title: Overview: Distances in separated point sets
content: The Erdős–Lovász–Vesztergombi conjecture (1997) states that among all $n$-point $1$-separated sets in $\mathbb{R}^2$ (pairwise distances $\ge 1$), the triangular lattice maximizes the number of pairs at distance $\le t$, for every $t\ge 1$. The problem is open in general. This entry formalizes the triangular-lattice shell counts, proves the planar kissing-number bound as the geometric engine, and settles the conjecture unconditionally for the base case $t=1$ (unit distances).
mathContext: Among $n$-point sets with pairwise distance $\ge 1$, does the triangular lattice maximize $\#\{$pairs at distance $\le t\}$ for all $t\ge 1$? Open; the $t=1$ case is proved here.

title: Imports and Namespace
content: Imports Mathlib's real number type, natural number basics, finite set operations, and cardinality. The `open Finset` command brings finite set notation (×ˢ for product, `.filter`, `.card`) into scope, supporting decidable computation over finite point configurations.
mathContext: Uses $\mathbb{R}$ for coordinates, $\mathbb{N}$ for counts, and $\text{Finset}$ for finite point sets with decidable membership and filtering.

title: Point2D: Points in the Plane
content: Defines Point2D as the product type ℝ × ℝ, representing points in the Euclidean plane. This is the ambient space for Erdős Problem #662. All point sets, distances, and lattice constructions operate over this type.
mathContext: Points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ form the ambient space. The choice of product type rather than $\text{EuclideanSpace}$ simplifies coordinate access for distance computations.

title: Squared Euclidean Distance
content: Defines the squared Euclidean distance between two plane points as (x₁ − x₂)² + (y₁ − y₂)². Using squared distance avoids square roots, simplifying algebraic manipulation and comparison. The separation and neighbor predicates are expressed in terms of squared distance throughout.
mathContext: $d^2(p, q) = (p_1 - q_1)^2 + (p_2 - q_2)^2$. Since $d^2$ is monotone in $d$ for $d \ge 0$, comparisons $d(p,q) \le t$ become $d^2(p,q) \le t^2$.

title: 1-Separated Point Set
content: A finite point set is 1-separated if all pairwise squared distances are at least 1, i.e., all pairwise Euclidean distances are at least 1. Equivalently, closed unit disks of radius 1/2 centered at the points are interior-disjoint. This is the fundamental constraint in Problem #662.
mathContext: A set $S \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ is **1-separated** if $d(p, q) \ge 1$ for all $p \ne q \in S$. Equivalently, $S$ is a **packing** with minimum distance 1. The densest such packing in $\mathbb{R}^2$ is the triangular lattice (Thue 1910, Tóth 1940).

title: Neighbors Within Distance t
content: The set of neighbors of a point p within squared distance t² (i.e., Euclidean distance ≤ t), excluding p itself. This is the local interaction neighborhood. The number of such neighbors per vertex is the key quantity bounded by the contact number in the t = 1 case.
mathContext: $N_t(p) = \{q \in S \setminus \{p\} : d(p,q) \le t\}$. For the triangular lattice, $|N_1(p)| = 6$, $|N_{\sqrt{3}}(p)| = 12$, $|N_3(p)| = 18$ (coordination shells).

title: Pair Count Functions
content: Defines orderedPairsWithinDist (counting ordered pairs (p,q) with p ≠ q and d(p,q) ≤ t) and pairsWithinDist (the unordered count, dividing by 2). The unordered pair count is the central quantity in the Erdős–Lovász–Vesztergombi conjecture.
mathContext: $\text{pairs}_t(S) = |\{\{p,q\} \subset S : d(p,q) \le t\}| = \frac{1}{2}\sum_{p \in S} |N_t(p)|$. The conjecture asserts $\text{pairs}_t(S) \le |S| \cdot f(t) / 2$ where $f(t) = |N_t(\mathbf{0})|$ in the triangular lattice.

title: Triangular Lattice and Lattice Count
content: Constructs the triangular (hexagonal) lattice in ℝ² with basis vectors (1, 0) and (1/2, √3/2), giving minimum distance 1. The lattice count function f(t) = triangularLatticeCount(t) gives the number of nonzero lattice points within distance t of the origin. This is axiomatized because computing it requires enumerating lattice shells.
mathContext: The **triangular lattice** $\Lambda = \mathbb{Z}(1,0) + \mathbb{Z}(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})$ has $f(t) = |\{(a,b) \in \mathbb{Z}^2 \setminus \{(0,0)\} : a^2 + ab + b^2 \le t^2\}|$. The squared norm $a^2 + ab + b^2$ is the Loeschian form, and $f(t)$ counts representations by this form.

title: Lattice Squared Distance Formula
content: The squared distance from a triangular lattice point (a, b) to the origin equals a² + ab + b². This is the Loeschian quadratic form, which classifies distances in the triangular lattice. Numbers representable by this form (Loeschian numbers: 0, 1, 3, 4, 7, 9, 12, 13, ...) are exactly those whose prime factorization has primes ≡ 2 (mod 3) appearing to even powers.
mathContext: $d^2((a, b), (0,0)) = a^2 + ab + b^2$ in the triangular lattice. This is the norm form of $\mathbb{Z}[\omega]$ where $\omega = e^{2\pi i/3}$, connecting to Eisenstein integers.

title: Known Lattice Shell Values
content: The triangular lattice has exactly 6 nearest neighbors at distance 1 (coordination number), 12 points within distance √3 (first two shells), and 18 within distance 3 (first several shells). These correspond to counting integer solutions of a² + ab + b² ≤ t² for the given values of t.
mathContext: $f(1) = |\{(a,b) \ne (0,0) : a^2+ab+b^2 \le 1\}| = 6$ (the 6 neighbors $\pm(1,0), \pm(0,1), \pm(1,-1)$). $f(\sqrt{3}) = 12$ adds the 6 second-shell points at $d^2 = 3$. The coordination sequence of the triangular lattice begins 1, 6, 6, 6, 6, ...

title: Unit Neighbor Bound (Contact Number)
content: In any 1-separated planar point set, each point has at most 6 neighbors at distance exactly 1. This is because the angular separation between unit-distance neighbors must be at least π/3 (by the triangle inequality and 1-separation), so at most 6 can fit around a point. This is the hexagonal kissing number in ℝ².
mathContext: For 1-separated $S \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ and $p \in S$: $|N_1(p)| \le 6$. Proof sketch: if $q, r \in N_1(p)$ with $q \ne r$, then $d(q,r) \ge 1$ and $d(p,q), d(p,r) \le 1$, so the angle $\angle qpr \ge \pi/3$. The 2D kissing number is 6.

title: Ordered Unit-Distance Pairs Bound
content: The total number of ordered unit-distance pairs in a 1-separated n-point set is at most 6n. This follows by summing the unit neighbor bound |N₁(p)| ≤ 6 over all p ∈ S. Combined with the unordered pair count (dividing by 2), this gives the contact number bound.
mathContext: $\sum_{p \in S} |N_1(p)| \le 6|S|$ by the per-vertex bound. The ordered pair count equals this sum, giving $|\{(p,q) : p \ne q,\, d(p,q) \le 1\}| \le 6n$.

title: Contact Number Bound (3n)
content: The number of unordered unit-distance pairs in a 1-separated n-point set is at most 3n. This is proved by dividing the ordered bound (6n) by 2 and applying omega. This is the t = 1 case of the Erdős–Lovász–Vesztergombi conjecture, and it is tight: the triangular lattice achieves 3n − O(√n).
mathContext: $\text{pairs}_1(S) = \frac{1}{2}\sum_{p \in S}|N_1(p)| \le 3n$. Harborth (1974) showed the exact maximum contact number is $\lfloor 3n - \sqrt{12n - 3}\rfloor$, achieved by hexagonal configurations.

title: Erdős–Lovász–Vesztergombi Conjecture (OPEN)
content: The main conjecture (Problem #662): for every t ≥ 1, among all sufficiently large 1-separated point sets in ℝ², the triangular lattice maximizes the number of pairs at distance ≤ t. The formulation requires N large enough (to avoid boundary effects in finite lattice patches). Axiomatized because the conjecture is open.
mathContext: For all $t \ge 1$, $\exists N$ such that $\forall S \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ 1-separated with $|S| \ge N$: $\text{pairs}_t(S) \le |S| \cdot f(t)/2$. The $t = 1$ case (contact number) is resolved; the general case remains open after 29 years.

title: Geometry of unit neighbors
content: The technical core studies, for a point $p$ in a $1$-separated set, its *unit neighbors* at exactly unit distance. Each such neighbor is a unit vector from $p$; converting to complex numbers, a unit vector has $\|z\|=1$ and its direction is captured by an argument normalized to $[0,2\pi)$. Two distinct unit neighbors subtend an angle $\ge \pi/3$: if $|\theta|<\pi/3$ then $\cos\theta>1/2$, but separation forces $\cos\theta\le 1/2$ (dot product $=\cos$ of the argument difference for unit vectors). This angular gap is the crux of the kissing bound.
mathContext: Unit neighbors are unit vectors; for distinct ones the angle $\theta$ satisfies $\cos\theta\le 1/2$, i.e. $|\theta|\ge\pi/3$. Dot product of unit vectors $=\cos(\arg z_1-\arg z_2)$.

title: The planar kissing number is 6
content: The angular gap $\ge\pi/3$ implies at most $\lfloor 2\pi/(\pi/3)\rfloor = 6$ unit vectors can be pairwise separated — the 2D kissing number bound `kissing_number_2d`. Applied pointwise, every point of a $1$-separated set has at most $6$ unit neighbors (`unit_neighbor_bound`), exactly matching the triangular lattice's $6$ nearest neighbors.
mathContext: At most $6$ pairwise-$\ge\pi/3$-separated unit vectors fit in $\mathbb{R}^2$; hence each point of a $1$-separated set has $\le 6$ unit neighbors, achieved by the triangular lattice.

title: The t = 1 case, unconditionally
content: Summing the per-point bound gives at most $6n$ ordered unit-distance pairs, hence at most $3n$ unordered ones (`contact_number_3n`). Since the triangular lattice attains $3n - O(\sqrt n)$ unit-distance pairs, it is optimal at $t=1$: `erdos_662_unit_case` proves the Erdős–Lovász–Vesztergombi conjecture unconditionally for unit distances, while the general threshold form remains an axiom (`erdos_662_lattice_optimal`).
mathContext: Ordered unit pairs $\le 6n$; unordered $\le 3n$; triangular lattice achieves $\approx 3n$, so it maximizes unit-distance pairs ($t=1$).
